# Generalizable Radiance Fields
Also called: Generalizable Neural Radiance Fields, Feedforward NeRF, View Synthesis Networks

## Overview
Generalizable Radiance Fields solve the problem of per-scene optimization latency by learning a data prior from a large-scale dataset, enabling immediate novel view synthesis on unseen scenes without iterative training [S1]. They differ from standard [radiance-field optimization](#44-radiance-field-optimization.md) methods by replacing per-scene gradient descent with a feedforward neural network that aggregates multi-view features or cost volumes to predict density and color directly [S1].

## Shared principles
Generalizable radiance fields share the goal of bypassing per-scene optimization by learning a representation from a large-scale dataset that can be adapted to unseen objects or scenes [S1]. This is achieved by learning generalizable geometric priors from source images, typically obtained using feature volumes or transformer-based attention modules to aggregate source view information [S1]. Recent methods also leverage deep multiview stereo (MVS) strategies to enforce generalization within the [NeRF](#1185-nerf-neural-radiance-fields.md) or 3D [Gaussian Splatting](#946-gaussian-splatting.md) pipelines [S1].

## Subtopics

### [NeRF-SDP](8554-nerf-sdp.md)
[NeRF-SDP](#8554-nerf-sdp.md) is an efficient generalizable [neural radiance field](#834-neural-radiance-field-nerf.md) that achieves high-fidelity novel view synthesis using sparse sampling points by incorporating scene depth perception via geometry feature extraction and a depth-encoded ray transformer [8554-nerf-sdp]. It solves the problem of balancing rendering speed and quality in generalizable NeRFs, where existing methods either rely on complex networks that are inefficient or use simpler networks/fewer sampling points that lead to artifacts [8554-nerf-sdp]. It differs from standard NeRFs by replacing per-ray MLP optimization with a differentiable 3D convolutional encoding of a pre-computed cost volume and from other generalizable methods by explicitly using monocular depth estimation for geometry features and a depth-encoded ray transformer to maintain quality with fewer sampling points [8554-nerf-sdp].

### [IBRNet](9383-ibrnet.md)
[IBRNet](#9383-ibrnet.md) is a feedforward neural network for generalizable view synthesis that bypasses per-scene optimization by learning a data prior from a training set [9383-ibrnet]. It differs from [standard NeRF](#979-nerf-volumetric-rendering-coarse-fine-sampling.md) by using a CNN to extract multi-view features and a Ray Transformer to predict density, enabling inference on unseen scenes without iterative training [9383-ibrnet].

### Generalizable Radiance Fields via Feature Volumes
A generalizable approach aiming to learn a representation from a large-scale dataset that can be fine-tuned for unseen objects, using feature volumes to obtain generalizable geometric priors [S1].

## Background
Original implicit radiance field representations lack cross-scene generalization capabilities and typically overlook relations between views, requiring long per-scene optimization [S1]. To mitigate this, methods following a generalizable approach aim to learn a representation from a large-scale dataset that can be fine-tuned and adapted to unseen objects or scenes [S1]. This is achieved by learning generalizable geometric priors from source images, obtained using feature volumes or transformer-based attention modules to aggregate source view information [S1]. Recent methods further enforce generalization by leveraging deep multiview stereo (MVS) strategies incorporated into the original NeRF and 3D Gaussian Splatting pipelines [S1].
